rules.prepare:
# As in Debian's rules. cd "$AELTRA_SOURCE_DIR" AM_OPTS=--copy LT_OPTS=--copy ./autogen.sh
# The options of Debian's rules, with these differences: no systemd, no # udev and no cryptsetup, which are not there, and at the end the options # that Debian does not have (no NLS, no bash completion). cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" $AELTRA_SOURCE_DIR/configure \ --prefix="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX" \ --libdir="$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX/lib" \ --build="$AELTRA_HOST_TYPE" \ --host="$AELTRA_HOST_TYPE" \ --enable-usrdir-path \ --with-ntfs-mounttype=ntfs \ --disable-makeinstall-chown \ --with-selinux \ --with-smack \ --enable-partx \ --without-systemd \ --without-udev \ --with-audit \ --without-cryptsetup \ --enable-newgrp \ --enable-login \ --enable-nologin \ --disable-mesg \ --disable-write \ --without-python \ --disable-kill \ --disable-chfn-chsh \ --disable-cal \ --disable-last \ --disable-utmpdump \ --disable-hwclock-gplv3 \ --disable-nls \ --disable-bash-completion
# During the first phase of package builds during bootstrapping, the build # system finds /tools/include/ncurses and adds /tools/include to the header # search path even when the prefix has been set to /usr. To work around that # we fix up all files with /tools/include inside before running the build.
if [ "$AELTRA_BUILD_FOR" = "target" ] && [ -d /tools/include/ncurses ]; then sed -i "s@/tools/include@/usr/include@g" $( grep -r -l -F "/tools/include" * | sort -u ) fi
rules.build:
if [ "$AELTRA_BUILD_FOR" = "tools" ]; then export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR/.libs" fi
cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" make -j"$AELTRA_PARALLEL_JOBS"
rules.install:
install -d -m 0755 $AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/usr install -d -m 0755 $AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/usr/bin install -d -m 0755 $AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/usr/sbin install -d -m 0755 $AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/usr/lib
ln -sf usr/bin "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/bin" ln -sf usr/sbin "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/sbin"
cd "$AELTRA_BUILD_DIR" make DESTDIR="$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR" install
rm -f "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/bin" rm -f "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/sbin"
# What follows is what Debian's packaging does with the installed files # (rules, *.install, *.links, not-installed, debputy.manifest). cd "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/$AELTRA_INSTALL_PREFIX"
# Not installed: libtool files, the static libraries other than libuuid # and libblkid, and three programs. rm -f lib/*.la lib/security/*.la rm -f lib/libfdisk.a lib/liblastlog2.a lib/libmount.a lib/libsmartcols.a rm -f bin/irqtop bin/setpgid bin/uname26
# These are in the program folder of users in Debian. for PROG in addpart blkzone chcpu delpart ldattach partx pivot_root \ resizepart switch_root; do mv "sbin/$PROG" bin/ done
# rename is the one of Perl in Debian. mv bin/rename bin/rename.ul
ln -s agetty sbin/getty ln -s hexdump bin/hd ln -s newgrp bin/sg
# su, mount, umount and newgrp are setuid root in Debian. The package files # say so (mode="4755"), whatever the makefile does here.
# Debian's PAM files, see package.xml. install -d -m 0755 "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/pam.d" share/pam-configs for NAME in login remote; do case "$NAME" in login) SRC="login.pam" ;; *) SRC="login.$NAME.pam" ;; esac install -m 644 "$AELTRA_WORK_DIR/extra/$SRC" \ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/pam.d/$NAME" done for NAME in runuser runuser-l su su-l; do install -m 644 "$AELTRA_WORK_DIR/extra/util-linux.$NAME.pam" \ "$AELTRA_INSTALL_DIR/etc/pam.d/$NAME" done install -m 644 "$AELTRA_WORK_DIR/extra/pam-configs/lastlog2" \ share/pam-configs/
